There is growing uncertainty over the leadership of the Lagos Waste Management Authority following reports that the state government has asked its Managing Director, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin, to resign, amid persistent heaps of refuse across parts of the state. PUNCH Online exclusively reported that Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu asked Gbadegesin to step down over the worsening waste management situation. There were indications that a replacement was immediately appointed. However, as of the time of filing this report, the Lagos State Government had yet to issue an official statement confirming Gbadegesin’s removal or the appointment of a successor. When contacted on Tuesday, the state Commissioner for Information, Gbenga Omotoso, said he was not aware of the development. He said, “I am not aware of the removal. I only saw it on your paper today. I have been busy attending meetings. You can call me tomorrow.” A top official of the Ministry of the Environment, who spoke on condition of anonymity, also told PUNCH Metro on Tuesday that he didn’t know about the LAWMA MD’s removal and replacement. He said, “Me, I don’t know o. Nothing is confirmed yet. I am sure an official statement will come from the ministry.” All other efforts to get the confirmation of LAWMA proved abortive as the agency’s Director of Publicity, Olabamiji Sanusi, did not pick up his calls nor respond to the message sent to him as of press time. The waste management crisis has affected several communities, including Mushin, Egbeda, Surulere, Ajegunle, Ikorodu, Ojo, Obalende, Apapa and Mile 2, where residents have had to contend with heaps of decomposing waste. The situation also raised concerns about environmental sanitation, public health and the impact of poor waste collection on businesses and the state’s image. PUNCH Online reported that an insider within LAWMA, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Sanwo-Olu had become increasingly dissatisfied with Gbadegesin’s handling of the crisis and had advised him to resign. According to the source, the governor’s displeasure followed concerns over the slow pace of waste evacuation and the agency chief’s alleged failure to act promptly on directives to address the situation. He gave instructions that immediate action be taken on the matter, as he has declared a state of emergency on waste management. “The governor was upset when he observed that the situation had not improved despite his clear directive. So, over the weekend, he asked him to resign, although he is begging and has reached out to some prominent Lagosians to beg on his behalf,” the source was quoted as saying. In September, PUNCH Online reported that Sanwo-Olu declared a state of emergency on waste collection after inspecting the Olusosun dumpsite in Ojota, where he directed that immediate measures be taken to tackle challenges affecting the sector. The governor, accompanied by his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, met with stakeholders in the waste management sector at the dumpsite to assess the challenges affecting municipal waste collection and outline immediate, medium- and long-term solutions. Sanwo-Olu acknowledged the slow pace of waste collection across the state, attributing the situation partly to the failure of Private Sector Participation operators to meet their obligations in the preceding weeks. However, the accumulation of refuse in several communities has continued to attract complaints despite the government’s intervention. Meanwhile, Gbadegesin, in a weekly update on waste management posted on his X handle on Saturday, said the authority had intensified clearance operations in some areas and deployed additional trucks to improve collection. He said Mile 2 had been cleared, with routine collection sustained, while three additional trucks were deployed to Doyin-Orile and its environs. “Eleven of the 15 routes in this week’s programme now have field updates. Key outcomes include: Mile 2 cleared with routine collection sustained; three additional trucks deployed on Doyin-Orile; daily service maintained on Ijesha Road and Itire-Ikate; Bucknor-Ijegun cleared with three-times-weekly collection. “Okeira and Oluodo are under LAWMA interim service following PSP termination; collection is sustained at Ogolonto and Igbokusu; Obalende has been cleared, provided with a bin and placed under surveillance; and clearance continues at Iraye,” he wrote. Gbadegesin added that four routes—Apapa, Abesan Estate, Idimu-Ejigbo Road and the Isheri-Igando corridor—were still awaiting field updates. “The objective is to progress from clearance to sustained collection and prevention of recurrence, not simply remove visible waste,” he stated.
